name: Simmonds-Moore sham God Helmet: 30 min relaxation, inert helmet (no field)
origin: Christine Simmonds-Moore, D. L. Rice, C. O'Gwin & R. Hopkins (sham-helmet study, Imagination, Cognition and Personality)
summary: The sham-helmet study of Simmonds-Moore et al.: paranormal sceptics and believers (32 and 35 in the abstract, 32 and 36 in the method section) relaxed for 30 min in a darkened Faraday chamber, once without a helmet and twice wearing an inert 'God Helmet'. No field was applied; the paper reports more exceptional experiences in believers. This program keeps the coils silent.
notes: Simmonds-Moore 2017: three 30-min sessions per person in counterbalanced order, a baseline without a helmet and a morning sham session, both at 10 a.m., and an afternoon sham session at 5 p.m. (p.15). The sham helmet was a red motorcycle helmet with eight telephone-microphone suction cups glued in, four per side over the temporal area, cabled to two USB splitters whose blue lights showed the system switched on (p.15-16). Participants were told the study 'explores the influence of mild electromagnetic stimulation on relaxation and human experiences', wore an eye mask and ear plugs (p.17) and relaxed in a reclining chair in a darkened chamber (p.20). Field-meter readings were taken within their sight 'to maximize participant expectations' (p.17). 68 people completed all three sessions, 32 sceptics and 36 believers (p.15); the abstract has 32 and 35 (p.1). This program plays nothing: every coil stays silent for 30 min, the same output as sham, and the intensity setting has no effect. It copies the exposure, not the belief that the helmet is on. Ticking Blind on this file changes nothing, since both arms are silent. For a blinded test, run an active 30-min program with the Blind option, or let a helper choose in secret between this file and an active program of the same length. Support: one study with no field arm. Reported: believers scored higher than sceptics on some inventory dimensions and reported more exceptional experiences; the condition did not change the inventory scores. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). If you run this for someone else, say beforehand that the helmet may or may not produce a field, and reveal it afterwards. Unpleasant feelings can come from the setting alone; stop on distress.
setting: Relaxing in a reclining chair for 30 min in a quiet, darkened, shielded room (the original used a Faraday chamber), with an eye mask and ear plugs, the helmet worn but inert; the baseline session is in the same room without the helmet.
schedule: Three sessions per person in counterbalanced order: baseline (no helmet) and the morning sham-helmet session at 10 a.m., the afternoon sham-helmet session at 5 p.m.
source: Simmonds-Moore, Rice, O'Gwin & Hopkins, Exceptional experiences following exposure to a sham 'God Helmet': evidence for placebo, individual difference, and time of day influences, Imagination, Cognition and Personality 39:44-87 (online 2017) https://doi.org/10.1177/0276236617749185 ; Psi Encyclopedia (SPR), Christine Simmonds-Moore (dummy helmet; baseline without a helmet; no morning/afternoon difference) https://psi-encyclopedia.spr.ac.uk/articles/christine-simmonds-moore/ ; Maij & van Elk 2018, Conscious Cogn 66:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30355534/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
